newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran urges EU states not to risk ties over verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges EU states not to risk ties over verdict.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Friday urged European Union states not to jeopardise their interests in Iran over a German court's verdict that Tehran ordered political killings in Germany.

"Our advice to Germany and other countries is not to tie their long-term political and economic interests in Iran, in this region and in the Islamic world to the remarks of an infamous judge of a local court," Velayati said.

He was responding to a question about Iran's reaction to the EU's call for member states to withdraw their ambassadors from Tehran over the Berlin court ruling that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Germany.
"They (EU states) should know that we are determined to answer any negative or positive moves swiftly and firmly," Velayati told Iranian state television.

"They should not act unwisely and lose their balance over these controversies. Iran is watching the other states' actions carefully and...the future of ties with these countries will be determined by their attitude towards us," he said.
Iran has repeatedly denied all involvement in the killings which it blames on infighting among opposition groups.
Germany, one of Iran's main trade partners, withdrew its ambassador from Tehran and asked four Iranian diplomats to leave. Iran also recalled its ambassador and expelled four German diplomats.
EU members, with the exception of Greece, recalled their envoys for consultations following Thursday's verdict.
Switzerland said its ambassador to Iran was in Berne and would be kept there while it decides how to respond.
The court decision forced the EU to abandon its controversial "critical dialogue" with Iran in a move which delighted the United States and other opponents of Tehran's Islamic government.
